body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #12 and #13. Reading-order recovery has improved, but eliminating `reading_order_unresolved` does not establish exact recovery of real-world revisions. Replacements remain missed, unchanged characters can appear in change spans, and ambiguous edit locations prevent acceptance even when paragraph correspondence is supplied.

Reconsider correspondence and exact-change acceptance together, starting with frozen counterexamples. The latest experiments do not support continuing to add recovery candidates or relax thresholds without revisiting the acceptance contract.

## Published baseline: PR #13

These results are committed at `3bebfeb`, independently of the later local experiments below:

- The five targeted revision pairs no longer have expected-change failures attributed to `reading_order_unresolved`, but the CSF replacement remains unmatched. Finding its old/new quotes separately as deletion/insertion does not establish replacement recall.
- For the reviewed CSF Core sentence, unchanged characters are included in change spans; scoped event coordinates remain indeterminate, and reviewed relation recall is 1/3.
- The SP 800-53 Approved comma replacement is not classified correctly; footer recovery is 150/157. Its original scoped quality baseline is unavailable.
- CSAF and both IRS form scopes retain zero scoped recall. IRS 1040 coverage decreases from 0.516980/0.490659 to 0.506352/0.486039 (old/new).
- Published validation reports 1,988 passing tests and 48/48 generated cases. This alone does not establish practical-release readiness on real documents.

Published evidence:

- [Acceptance status](https://github.com/hayatosc/pdfdelta/blob/3bebfeb/benchmark/realworld/results/issue12-anchor-recovery/acceptance-status.md)
- [Annotated precision comparison](https://github.com/hayatosc/pdfdelta/blob/3bebfeb/benchmark/realworld/results/issue12-anchor-recovery/annotated-precision-comparison.json)
- [Acceptance evidence](https://github.com/hayatosc/pdfdelta/blob/3bebfeb/benchmark/realworld/results/issue12-anchor-recovery/acceptance-evidence.json)

## Subsequent local experiments — not part of PR #13

These findings come from uncommitted work on 2026-09-08. They must not be presented as the merged baseline. Preserve minimal fixtures and reproducible commands before relying on these measurements for follow-up implementation.

A common assessment over 127 sources, followed by local comparison and all-optimal-alignment uniqueness checks, recovered only 1 of 25 reviewed target changes:

| Revision pair | Accepted target changes |
| --- | ---: |
| NIST CSF | 0/3 |
| NIST FIPS 186-4 to 186-5 | 0/7 |
| ECMA | 0/3 |
| NIST SP 800-53 | 1/8 |
| EDPB | 0/4 |

Two unchanged interior spaces were still counted as changed in an SP punctuation/case edit (`. F` to `; f`). Some searches exhausted their work budget. The experimental strict generated matrix was 42/48, although the five core acceptance cases and 2,067 tests passed. These experiments are therefore not a validated replacement for the published implementation.

### Better correspondence alone is insufficient

A FIPS DSA feasibility probe supplied a counterfactual, trusted whole-introduction boundary that the engine had not established itself. It produced an insertion candidate covering the reviewed quote but accepted none of its 74 candidates because their edit locations remained ambiguous. Search completed using 9,259,464 of a 32,000,000 work budget.

An exact LCS witness for that introduction has length 1,097 and edit cost 1,746. Equally optimal scripts can either insert the entire 107-character quote or align 33 of its characters, including non-whitespace characters, with old text. A paragraph-only probe also accepted no candidates; even an insertion boundary permits equal-cost alternatives such as ` no longer` versus `no longer `.

This shows a conflict between the current scalar-edit uniqueness criterion and some reviewed paragraph-level changes. It does not prove PDF comparison is impossible or that annotations are wrong. A revised contract must explain which evidence establishes a change and how competing interpretations are represented.

Local artifacts to preserve (currently uncommitted):

- `benchmark/realworld/results/2026-09-08-common-assessment/`
- `benchmark/realworld/results/2026-09-08-issue12-local-comparison/`
- `benchmark/realworld/results/2026-09-08-issue12-dsa-feasibility/`
- `fixtures/issue12/`

## Work required

- [ ] Freeze small source-backed reproducers for missed replacements, unchanged characters inside change spans, and DSA equal-cost alternatives. Record inputs, commands, implementation revision, and expectations.
- [ ] Define and review established versus ambiguous change acceptance, including how paragraph-level evidence interacts with multiple optimal scalar edit scripts. Validate on these counterexamples before expanding recovery heuristics.
- [ ] Improve old/new region correspondence while retaining glyph provenance, reversible layout, and exact reconstruction. Do not treat externally supplied boundaries as engine-established evidence.
- [ ] Correct source-coordinate accounting and false-positive measurement, including unchanged whitespace inside accepted events. Preserve accounting for failed, unsupported, unresolved, partial, and budget-limited comparisons.
- [ ] Re-evaluate published residual cases. Report accepted-change recall, unchanged-character false positives, coverage, and search completion separately. Keep form-heavy failures visible; deferred work needs a linked follow-up rather than disappearing from the denominator.

## Acceptance criteria

- The documented contract explains the DSA counterexample and yields either a justified source-backed change or explicit unresolved ambiguity, without manufacturing certainty by selecting an arbitrary optimal script.
- Recovery improves on a frozen reviewed baseline without increasing unchanged-character false positives. Publish per-case counts and remaining misses; do not edit annotations merely to make the implementation pass.
- All five practical-release core cases remain required: line-wrap invariance, page-break invariance, exact single replacement, exact single paragraph insertion, and exact single paragraph deletion.
- Resolve generated-matrix regressions or justify them individually against the documented contract. Passing unit tests alone is insufficient.
- Validate generalization on a genuinely unseen holdout after using current examples for development. Previously inspected documents must not be relabeled as unseen.
- Preserve parser limits, uncertainty handling, and the raw evidence → imperfect structure → robust alignment → exact diff pipeline.
title: Redesign exact-change acceptance and recover remaining real-world revisions
